comment: Not the worst professor, but not the best. He can be unaccommodating and sarcastic, but varies day to day.

Took this over the summer and it was so doable. Video assignments are sent each week. Make sure to take notes because the material on exams come from these videos. Very nice professor and knowledgeable. Reach out to him if you have any questions, he is very accessible!

SIMPLY RUN! there are easier gen eds out there. His lectures are boring, he does not share his slides and his tests are like 40 points (if you get one thing wrong it really affects your grade, and you need to get an answer 100% right for it to count. HE DOESN'T DO PARTIAL CREDIT).

Not a bad choice for your art gen ed but not the best one either. You'll spend the class watching jazz videos and doing some music 101. Music people will find it easy peasy, the rest may have a harder time even though Dr. Esleck will try to make it fair for everybody. A lot of information to learn for the exams, which will only come from your notes

Otherwise known as The Jazz Tradition. Anyone who needs to fulfill their art requirement and is terrible at the arts should take Esleck. Class time is spent listening to various jazz recordings and learning about the history of jazz. Just remember to take detailed notes on everything he says, as test questions come directly from lectures.
David Esleck is one of the best professors I’ve had. The jazz class is great even if is early. Hard to get in his class, though. Esleck is very popular.
Not as easy as everyone makes him out to be but not to hard either. Very nice guy. Test can be hard and random but he gives other opportunities to get credit

Dr. Esleck was probably the only teacher I've had at Richmond that I've been truly disappointed with. Although he does know jazz well and is talented, he doesn't engage the class or make learning the material in any way meaningful. He is very hard to get in touch with outside of class, and makes it seem that class is not his priority.

Even if you do poorly on tests Dr. Esleck gives you a chance to get an A in the class as long as you participate and do a bunch of extra credit essays which are just a one page review of a jazz preformance and it gives you 5 points on a test.  So just do a bunch of those

Easy class.  A great class. Makes people learn to like music but doesn't pound it down your throat. Very musically talented. Go to concerts for extra credit and get ready for a 4.0 in this class. All that Jazz with him is another great class.  Recommend both!!!
Esleck is great, he is amazingly talented too. the 8:15 will kill u, but theres no homework, and its a pretty easy course. it actually made me like jazz.

Esleck is great guy with a passion for jazz.  He really makes an effort to know his students and make sure you understand jazz.  The class is easy and fun, even with little interest in the music. He obviously has fun with his class and even at 815 I enjoy being there.

Incredibly easy course.  Good way to get your music requirement out of the way.  He's a great teacher with a huge passion for jazz... easy even if you have absolutely no prior experience with jazz or music
He teaches well, the class is great if you have any interest in Jazz Music.  Very easy, even if you have no experience with music before.
